scope: Rebuild the Command Center in Blender using art/blender/command-center/references/command-center-concept.png as the primary visual authority.
Treat existing Blender geometry as disposable visual implementation; preserve only protected runtime/spatial anchors.
Use Codex vision plus Blender/Blender Python in an iterative reference -> build -> render -> compare -> correct loop.
Prioritize major silhouette, depth, curved architecture, facade articulation, material separation, landscape, human-scale cues and floating-platform form before small detail.
Stop at REFERENCE REBUILD — HUMAN VISUAL REVIEW READY. Do not export GLB or modify React.
acceptance: Primary visual authority is command-center-concept.png; secondary references may inform atmosphere only.
Player spawn, bridge interfaces, Ask clearance, walkable topology, world scale and runtime camera operating constraints remain unchanged.
Existing Massing V2 geometry is not protected visual composition and may be replaced wholesale.
The known legacy detail-pass object families are absent from the final EXPORT_COMMAND_CENTER collection.
The final scene is not dominated by very low-complexity primitive-like meshes; reference-rebuild-geometry validation passes.
At least three real runtime-camera intermediate renders are preserved under previews/reference-iterations and recorded in reference-comparison.json.
Each recorded iteration identifies the largest visible mismatch against the primary reference and the substantive correction made.

The runtime-camera render materially resembles the reference in silhouette, foreground/midground/background depth, vertical hierarchy, curvature, facade depth, material separation, landscape, human scale, floating-platform form and lighting hierarchy.
The final comparison grades silhouette, depth, curvature, facade_depth, materials, landscape, human_scale, floating_platform and lighting as close or minor_gap only.
The result does not read primarily as cubes, cylinders, toruses, repeated slabs or emissive trim decorating primitive massing.
Large visual mismatches are corrected before small-detail polish.
The editable command-center.blend is committed.
reference-runtime.png, reference-top.png and reference-side.png are committed.
reference-rebuild-review.md explicitly compares the final runtime render against the primary reference and lists remaining visible differences.
reference-rebuild-validation.json records source validation status and protected_anchors as unchanged.
reference-comparison.json records the exact primary reference path/SHA, real iteration renders and final visual-axis assessment.
Blender source validation passes without weakening protected-clearance rules.
reference-rebuild-geometry, reference-rebuild-evidence and icm-stage validations pass.
No production GLB export occurs.
No React/runtime, CSP, decoder, topology, content, main or deployment change occurs.
Independent reviewer finds no protected-state violation; human visual approval remains mandatory before any export task.
stop_conditions: The trusted feature branch head no longer equals the task base SHA.
The primary reference image is unavailable or unreadable.
Matching the reference would require moving protected spawn, bridge interfaces, Ask clearance, topology or world scale.
Two materially similar rebuild approaches still produce a primitive/blocky visual language; stop and report the unresolved upstream visual constraint rather than adding another cosmetic pass.
The final geometry still contains known legacy detail-pass object families or fails the primitive-dominance heuristic.
Three real reference/render/correction iterations cannot be produced.
Any final visual comparison axis remains a major mismatch.
Blender source validation cannot pass without weakening protected spatial rules.
Any path outside the declared write scope changes.
Any GLB export, React/runtime edit, main change or deployment is attempted.
